name: Water Images
shortcutSummary: In a water image, top and bottom are reversed, but left and right stay the same. Imagine the figure reflected in water below it — it flips vertically (upside down).
conceptExplanation:
Water Image questions ask you to identify the reflection of a figure as seen in water. The rule: a horizontal mirror (water surface) reverses top-bottom, while left-right remains unchanged.

For letters: flip upside down. Letters like B, C, D, E, H, I, K, O, X look the same in water reflection.

subtopics.name: Water Images — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation:
Water Image questions ask you to identify the reflection of a figure as seen in water. The rule: a horizontal mirror (water surface) reverses top-bottom, while left-right remains unchanged.

For letters: flip upside down. Letters like B, C, D, E, H, I, K, O, X look the same in water reflection.
shortcuts: Horizontal Flip Rule: Only top-bottom reverses. Left-right stays same.
Upside-Down Test: Imagine turning the figure upside down — that's the water image.
Combined Mirror+Water: If asked for both, first flip horizontally (mirror), then vertically (water) = 180° rotation.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Choose the correct water image of the given word from the options:

FROST
options: Original word FROST unaltered
Both vertically and horizontally inverted (180° rotation)
Water image of FROST (vertically flipped top-to-bottom without changing left-to-right sequence)
Mirror image of FROST (laterally flipped left-to-right)
practiceQuestions.hint: Water image inverts Top and Bottom; sequence of letters does NOT reverse.
practiceQuestions.explanation: In water reflection, the reflection plane is horizontal (at the bottom). Top and bottom invert, but the left-to-right order of letters remains strictly unchanged: F R O S T (upside down; horizontal flip where F points downwards).
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Note that water reflection represents a horizontal mirror placed below the object.
Step 2: Top becomes Bottom, Bottom becomes Top.
Step 3: Left-to-right sequence remains unchanged (unlike mirror image).

practiceQuestions.questionText: A clock seen in water reflection shows the time as 4:20. What is the actual real time?
options: 2:10 (or 1:10 depending on hour hand overlap)
practiceQuestions.hint: Water clock formula: Subtract given time from 18:30 (or 17:90 if minutes > 30).
practiceQuestions.explanation: Formula for Water Image of Clock: Subtract from 18:30. Here: 18:30 - 4:20 = 14:10 = 2:10.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Note that water reflection represents a horizontal mirror placed below the object.
Step 2: Top becomes Bottom, Bottom becomes Top.
Step 3: Left-to-right sequence remains unchanged (unlike mirror image).
